What
A music track is read and decoded on a thread of its own, and the thread was
detached: nothing waited for it. The player can close the window while a track
is being read, and the program then exits (std::exit) with that thread still
running. The static destructors take the mutex and the stream list away under
it, and the thread locks a mutex that no longer exists: a crash at quit, which
the crash handler catches and writes a report for. The launcher then says the
game stopped unexpectedly,…

Summary

with all its bits, whatever type the C gives it in between. Where the
matched C relies on that, the port moved 8 of 16 bytes in quadword
copies, and passed colours and texture words to 64-bit parameters…

commits.headline: feat(launcher): Models and textures in short words, with Open folder
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The panel's words move to modsText.ts (ASSETS) and get shorter. After an
export, Open folder opens what it wrote again (api.openOutput, the job's

commits.headline: test(launcher): the job and AppImage tests no longer race their neighbours
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
cleans_appimage_python_environment set PYTHONHOME and APPDIR in the test
process itself, so any Python another test started meanwhile (the
installed copy's bundle_standalone.py) inherited a home that does not
exist and could not start. The AppImage's folder is now an argument.
The exit's folders come from stdout and stderr, read by two threads, so
their order is not defined: the test compares them sorted, and waits
longer under load.

commits.headline: fix(launcher): a link with several mods keeps its preview after one is installed
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
rac1-mods holds three mods, and Browse mods points at it, but installing
one closed the preview and emptied the link, so each of the others meant
pasting the link and Find again. With more than one mod the preview now
stays, the installed one's button at Reinstall; a link of one mod closes
as before.

commits.headline: fix(launcher): removing a mod, a pack or the set-up asks first on Linux
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
In the desktop app on Linux the page's confirm() answered yes without
showing anything (WebKitGTK under Tauri), so Remove on a gameplay mod
deleted it and its settings at once, and the same went for a pack, a GPU
driver, restoring a save backup, quitting the game and removing what a
disc set up. They ask through the dialog plugin now (api.ask, the
system's dialog, with the action on its button); the browser preview
keeps the page's confirm(). The window may show messages
(dialog:allow-message).
